children: A number of stocks fell in the afternoon session after AI-linked shares continued to pull back. Anthropic slid more than 10% following its debut, failing to revive confidence in the sector's spending boom.

Investors had looked to Anthropic's record $81.3 billion initial public offering and Nvidia's quarterly earnings beat under interim CEO Colette Kress to steady sentiment following Jensen Huang's resignation, CNBC reported. Instead, Anthropic's retreat toward its $83 offer price echoed Seaport Research warnings, covered by CNBC, that its valuation demands much faster revenue growth.

Separately, Federal Reserve Governor Lisa Cook warned against delaying rate hikes ahead of an expected December increase. Compounding the concerns, President Donald Trump threatened penalties on overseas U.S. data-center builds as new Commerce Department export-licensing rules weighed on chipmakers.
The stock market overreacts to news, and big price drops can present good opportunities to buy high-quality stocks.
Among others, the following stocks were impacted:
Electronic components & manufacturing company Coherent fell 14.6%. Is now the time to buy Coherent?

Coherent’s shares are extremely volatile and have had 91 moves greater than 5% over the last year. But moves this big are rare even for Coherent and indicate this news significantly impacted the market’s perception of the business.

The previous big move we wrote about was 1 day ago when the stock gained 0.6% on the news that the company's board of directors authorized a share repurchase program of up to $2.0 billion of its common stock.

According to a Form 8-K filing, Coherent's board approved the buyback authorization on November 18, 2026, and the $2.0 billion limit excludes fees, commissions or other expenses related to the repurchases. The Form 8-K also showed that the authorization permits Coherent to purchase its common stock from time to time in the open market or through negotiated purchases, including accelerated buyback programs. Coherent noted in the Form 8-K that the program has no expiration date, does not obligate the company to repurchase any specific number of shares and may be suspended or discontinued at any time.

Coherent is down 4.7% since the beginning of the year, and at $185.16 per share, it is trading 56.6% below its 52-week high of $426.89 from June 2026. Despite the year-to-date decline, investors who bought $1,000 worth of Coherent’s shares 5 years ago would now be looking at an investment worth $2,874.
